guard: a proof killed mid-mutation leaves a breadcrumb naming what it broke, and the next run or --recover puts the file back, bytes and timestamp, or refuses by naming the interrupted proof
why: A signal handler covers the kills that can be caught. SIGKILL cannot be, and it is the signal this
repo's own reproof harness sends to a proof that overruns its 140-minute budget
(`mutation-reproof.mjs`, `PROOF_TIMEOUT_MS` and `killSignal: "SIGKILL"`). The file such a proof
leaves is syntactically valid and deliberately sabotaged, every surface reports a clean checkout,
and the breadcrumb is the only thing that says otherwise.
Seven mutations for six properties, because each property is a separate way for the mechanism to
be present and useless, and each is repaired differently: the breadcrumb is never written, the
recovery never runs, a completed proof leaves its breadcrumb behind, the recovery puts the bytes
back but not the timestamp, a breadcrumb whose file already matches is treated as live, and a
mutation the tool cannot put back is measured instead of refused.
THE TIMESTAMP PAIR IS THE ONE WORTH ARGUING ABOUT, and it is two mutations for the reason
`restore-mtime.json` gives: a call that is gone and a call that writes the wrong time fail
differently. No byte comparison can see either. `smoke:dist-freshness` is an mtime ORDERING
test, so a recovered file whose timestamp is the time of the recovery makes it name a package
stale for a file nobody edited, which is the defect the happy path's `utimesSync` exists for.
THIS SUITE IS FAIL-FAST, so each mutation's named cell has to be the FIRST cell it reddens or
the verdict points at the wrong line. `a proof that completes leaves no breadcrumb behind` sits
right after the first completed proof for that reason: a leftover breadcrumb records the clean
hash of the file `a dirty tree is refused` then dirties, and that cell would redden first, for
the wrong reason.
NO top-level `completionMarker`, for the reason `restore-mtime.json` states about this same
suite: it is fail-fast, so its success banner is not printed on a red run, and a completion
marker pointed at it turns every genuine kill INCONCLUSIVE.
NOT ASSERTED, and recorded rather than implied: that a backup which does not hash to the
breadcrumb is refused before anything is written over the file. The recovery copies the backup
first and hashes the result afterwards, so there is no such check to mutate. Whether it should
check first is a question about the recovery's behaviour, raised on #1632 rather than settled
inside a coverage fixture.
